boundaries.label: features/<slice> — the module graph IS the architecture
Shared kernel — plain Java, no jakarta.*
State — one schema per slice, no cross-slice FK

cards.title: The module dependency rule
items: a module's pom.xml dependencies are the complete list of what it may import — a forbidden artifact fails Enforcer and compilation, and a domain module compiles with the plain maven-compiler-plugin, not a jakarta.* dependency
domain is plain Java: entities, value objects, rules and ports, with no jakarta.*, no JPA, no JAX-RS, no server API; presentation must not depend on adapters or JPA
one slice never imports another slice's entities, repositories or tables; a cross-slice read goes through the other slice's contracts and a port

cards.title: Ports and the composition root
items: the ports are named: WidgetRepository, Outbox, SessionStore, Clock, Notifier, TokenVerifier, PermissionChecker — a port uses domain types, so no EntityManager, HttpServletRequest or JMS type crosses into the domain

apps/api and apps/worker build the CDI graph; a producer returns the port type, not the implementation; the use case receives its ports through the constructor — no field injection, no service locator
tests build the same graph with fakes and the use case never changes: JUnit 5 for the use case, Weld SE for CDI, Testcontainers for PostgreSQL and Artemis

cards.title: Transactions and identity
items: the use case owns the JTA transaction and the resource and the repository never open one; the outbox row commits with the domain row; there is no XA — a distributed effect is an idempotent async job
@Version on every mutable aggregate: a conflict is a typed error mapped to 409, never a 500; expected failures are Result values, not exceptions
JPA entities live in adapters and never cross the API — the edge returns DTO records with Bean Validation, and one ExceptionMapper per error family maps to 401/403/404/409/422/429/5xx

cards.title: How the walls are enforced
items: Maven Enforcer and ArchUnit police the module graph; the Checkstyle config and the SpotBugs exclude file in lints/ police the code — the config wins when it and the prose disagree, and the prose is fixed

CI check.yml runs the skill validator, the Java-example balance gate, the unittest suite, and on a JDK the javac self-check plus the Checkstyle violation harness; lints/check/Clean.java must stay quiet while Violations.java keeps its deliberate findings

the contract is unbreakable and non-waivable: when a rule fires, re-cut the layout — never weaken, rename or delete the rule, and never silence it with a module-wide suppression; a config exception is a contract change
